1
RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Monday,  the July 24, 2006/Sravana 2, 1928 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Development of North Eastern Region; Food Processing Industries;
Human Resource Development; Law and Justice; Mines; Minority Affairs;
Non-Conventional Energy Sources; Ocean Development; Power; Science and
Technology; Social Justice and Empowerment; Tribal Affairs; Women and
Child Development)
Total number of questions — 20
Royalty on minerals
†*1. SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS: Will
the Minister of MINES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government of
Chhattisgarh have requested that royalty
on minerals be fixed on the basis of
percentage of its market value;
(b) whether Planning Commission have
also opined on the same lines;
(c) if so, the reasons for non-
implementation of the same; and
(d) the reasons for non-representation
of the producer-States in the Committee
constituted for this purpose?
Gap between consumption and
generation of power
*2. SHRI BALAVANT ALIAS BAL
APTE:
SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased
to state:
(a) the per capita gap between the
consumption and generation of power from
various sources in the country recorded
during the last three years, State-wise;
(b) the total quantum of power supplied
from Central pool to each State during the
period;
(c) whether the gap between
consumption and generation is likely to be
bridged during the ensuing five years;
(d) if so, the details thereof;
(e) the annual percentage of increase
being registered in power generation;
(f) whether it is a fact that the allocation
of funds for the current financial year has
been curtailed; and
(g) if so, the details thereof alongwith
the reasons therefor?
Strategy to balance demand and
supply of power
†*3. SHRI JANESHWAR MISHRA:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to
state:
 (a) whether Government have drawn
up any strategy for striking a balance
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

2
between the demand and  supply of power
in the country;
(b) whether Government have
formulated any concrete plan to end distress
being caused by the power crisis in the
national capital of the country; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Vacant posts and pending cases in
courts
*4. SHRI B.J. PANDA: Will the
Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Supreme Court has
directed all the State Governments and UTs
to draw out a schedule for timely filling up
of vacancies of judges to clear pending
litigations;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) what was the volume of pendency
of cases in the High Courts in 2005 and
how far it has increased since 2004?
Electrification of villages
*5. SHRI C. RAMACHANDRAIAH:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government have launched
'Rajiv Gandhi Grameen Vidyutikaran
Yojana' with an aim to provide electricity
to every home within five years;
(b) if so, the details thereof, particularly
in Andhra Pradesh;
(c) whether Government have drawn
any scheme to tap the available sources
of alternative energy to meet the set
targets;
(d) if so, the details thereof;
(e) the number of villages likely to be
covered for electrification in each State
during 2006-07;
(f) the allocation made for the same;
(g) the steps Government propose to
take to achieve the aim; and
(h) the role of NTPC, NHPC and Power
Grid Corporation under this programme?
Bio-mass energy for villages
*6. KUMARI NIRMALA DESH-
PANDE: Will the Minister of NON-
CONVENTIONAL ENERGY SOURCES
be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any proposal to
launch a mission for using bio-mass energy
for villages in a big way;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Groups to assist Oversight
Committee
*7. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the details of groups that have been
set up to assist Oversight Committee
which has been entrusted the work of
preparing a roadmap for implementation
of 27 per cent quota for OBCs in all
educational institutions;
(b) whether it is a fact that Government
have assured the Oversight Committee that
it would provide Rs. 4,000 crores for
expansion of infrastructure in educational
institutions where the reservation policy
is going to be implemented; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?

3
World Bank's report on election
expenditure
†*8. SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
Will the Minister of LAW AND
JUSTICE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the World
Bank has recently published a report
regarding expenses incurred by the
candidates in elections in the country;
(b) if so, whether it is also a fact that in
this report, the elections in India have been
termed as comparatively more expensive;
and
(c) if so, Government's reaction thereto
and the future proposals to check election
expenses?
Mineral reserves in the country
†*9. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
Will the Minister of MINES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government have made any
assessment recently regarding mineral
reserves in the country;
(b) if so, the total area where minerals
are likely to be found in the country; and
(c) the details of minerals and their
quantity expected to be available alongwith
the area in which the said minerals are likely
to be available?
Progress of electrification of villages
in Orissa
*10. SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN
PANY:
MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased
to state:
(a) the progress of electrification of
villages in Orissa under the Rajiv Gandhi
Grameen VidhyutikaranYojana;
(b) whether all the villages in the State
will be lighted up by 2009, the year fixed
by the Centre for covering all the villages in
the country under electrification; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Kendriya Vidyalayas in the country
*11. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is a proposal under
active consideration of the Union
Government to set up new Kendriya
Vidyalayas in the country;
(b) if so, the number thereof State-wise,
particularly, in Uttar Pradesh, and
(c) the details of such schools set up
during the last two years?
Legislation on OBC reservation
*12. SHRI SHANTARAM LAXMAN
NAIK: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government propose
to enact any legislation or a constitutional
amendment on OBC reservations in higher
education;
(b) if so, whether a draft legislation is
ready; and
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

4
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(c) if so, the essential features of the
legislation and by when the legislation is
likely to be introduced in Parliament?
Implementation of non-conventional
energy projects
*13. SHRI M.V. MYSURA REDDY:
Will the Minister of NON-
CONVENTIONAL ENERGY SOURCES
be pleased to state:
(a) whether funds are sanctioned to the
Nodal Agency of the State for
implementation of non-conventional energy
projects under V.E.S.P. (Village Energy
Security Programme) after ensuring a
certification from concerned Electricity
Board that these villages are not covered
under Rajiv Jyothi Electricity Programme;
(b) if so, how many projects have been
sanctioned in the country and whether
certification is ensured; and
(c) the amount allocated under Rajiv
Jyothi Electricity Programme for State
Electricity Boards?
Renovation of Indraprastha Power
Plant
†*14. SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
MS. SUSHILA TIRIYA:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the Ministry of
Environment and Forests has refused to
issue a ‘No Objection Certificate’ for
renovation of the Indraprastha Power Plant;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) the steps taken by Government to
eliminate the growing power crisis in Delhi
due to lack of renovation?
Increase in seats in higher studies
†*15. DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have taken a decision to increase the seats
in higher educational institutions to nullify
the ill-effects as a result of implementation
of the proposal providing reservation in
the field of higher education to backward
classes;
(b) if so, in which areas of higher
education Government have assessed the
requirement for increasing additional seats
and in what numbers; and
(c) Government's future plan regarding
this issue?
Mauda Thermal Power Plant in
Nagpur
*16. SHRIMATI  SYEDA
ANWARA TAIMUR:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased
to refer to the answer to Starred Question
275 given in the Rajya Sabha on the 9th
March, 2006 and state:
(a) whether Government have since
revisited the issue relating to setting up of
1000 MW coal-based Mauda Thermal
Power Plant in Nagpur; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?

5
Drug abuse in North-East
*17. SHRI C. PERUMAL: Will the
Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE AND
EMPOWERMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether a report of the United
Nations released recently, has said that drug
abuse in North-Eastern India, especially
among the youth is a cause for worry;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the action taken to prevent drug
abuse in North-East?
Reservation in private sector
*18. SHRI K. CHANDRAN PILLAI:
Will the Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE
AND EMPOWERMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) whether decrease of employment
opportunities in the Government/PSUs has
affected the sections enjoying reservation
of jobs;
(b) if so, whether Government
contemplate to bring new legislation for
providing reservation in jobs in private
sector;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Operation of Mid-Day meal by NGOs/
contractors
*19. MISS MABEL REBELLO: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the metropolitan cities in which Mid-
Day meals are managed by NGOs
alongwith the names of cities, NGO/
contractor and the number of children they
are giving meals;
(b) the NGOs giving Mid-Day meal to
the children in the tribal areas alongwith
the names of States, Districts, blocks and
number of children who get meals from the
NGOs;
(c) whether Government are
contemplating to operate Mid-Day meal
scheme through contractors as well; and
(d) the difference in quality of meal and
services offered by the contractors and
NGOs?
Additional power generation capacity
†*20. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that about 2000
MW additional power could be generated
in the Eastern and North Eastern region of
the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that this
additional power is not being utilised in the
power-stricken Northern region; and
(d) if so, the reasons therefor?
NEW DELHI; YOGENDRA NARAIN,
The 18th July, 2006 Secretary-General.
Asadha 27, 1928 (Saka)
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

1
RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for WRITTEN ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Monday,  the July 24, 2006/Sravana 2, 1928 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Development of North Eastern Region; Food Processing Industries;
Human Resource Development; Law and Justice; Mines; Minority Affairs;
Non-Conventional Energy Sources; Ocean Development; Power;
Science and Technology; Social Justice and Empowerment;
Tribal Affairs; Women and Child Development)
Total number of questions — 75
Setting-up of Food Processing Units
in rural and urban areas
1. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN: Will
the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) the details of subsidies/grants
available for setting-up food processing
units in rural/urban areas, separately;
(b) whether it is a fact that subsidies/
grants in respect of certain industries have
been withdrawn recently;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Policy for betterment of FPIs and
Agri-business
2. SHRI T.S.BAJWA: Will the Minister
of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Empowered
Committee of Ministers had approved the
policy for the betterment of food processing
industries and Agri-business;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the areas in which the intending
entrepreneurs are likely to be benefited?
Setting-up of food parks in Uttaranchal
†3. SHRI  HARISH RAWAT: Will the
Minister of FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government of Uttaranchal
has submitted any proposal to his Ministry
with regard to setting-up of food parks;
(b) if so,  the details thereof;
(c) whether his Ministry is considering
any proposal to increase the amount of
Central subsidy to be provided for
construction of food parks; and
(d) if so, the amount proposed to be
fixed for the same?
Central status to Utkal University
4. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN
PANY:
SHRI B. J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

2
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(a) whether it is proposed to grant
Central status to the Utkal University in
Orissa;
(b) if so, the status of the proposal; and
(c) the time-frame within which this
would be done to meet the aspirations of
the people of Orissa?
Establishment of schools for equal
opportunity
†5. SHRI  RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the attention of
Government has been drawn to the
statement of Deputy Chairman of National
Knowledge Commission in which it has
been stated that in the next  10-15 years,
if four lakh additional schools are started,
everybody can get an opportunity;
(b) if so, whether it is a fact that a scheme
has been formulated to implement this
proposal; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Non-essentiality  of NET for
lecturership
†6. SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
MS. SUSHILA TIRIYA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the
University Grants Commission has decided
to do away with the essentiality of the
compulsory National Eligibility Test
(NET) for filling up the vacant posts of
Lecturers in the Universities;
(b) whether a delegation of academicians
met the Prime Minister and the Human
Resource Development Minister in this
matter;
(c) if so,  whether any positive steps
have been taken by Government after this
meeting; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Differential fee structure
7. SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are considering
to introduce a differential fee structure to
suit the paying capacity of every student;
(b) whether Government has received
any recommendations in this regard;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) whether it is a fact that it would not
be prudent to charge the same fee from all
students irrespective of their socio-
economic status?
Higher education as pro-rich and
urban phenomenon
8. SHRIMATI  S.G. INDIRA: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that according to
a report it has been found that higher
education is a pro-rich and urban
phenomenon;
(b) if so, the steps being taken by
Government to remove this disparity; and
(c) whether it is also a fact that the
enrolment of the SCs in higher education

3
increased  from 8.6 per cent in  1990-91 to
11.3 per cent in 2002-03 while that of the
STs was from 2.1 per cent to 3.6 per cent?
Unrecognized technical and
professional courses
9. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that many
institutions all over India are offering degree
in technical and professional courses which
are not recognised by Government but have
credential in private sector;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether there is any plan to include
such courses in Government institutions
or universities or give affiliations to selected
private institutions so that students are free
from uncertainty about their future career
prospects; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Approval, recognition and accredition
to management courses
10. DR. M.A.M. RAMASWAMY:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to set
up a new body to grant approval,
recognition and accredition to management
courses thus making AICTE the sole body
to grant approval and recognition to
technical institutions only;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Maintaining staff-student ratio in
technical and management
institutions
11. DR. M.A.M. RAMASWAMY:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that most of the
technical and management institutions given
accredition by the All India Council of
Technical Education (AICTE) have not
been maintaining proper staff-student ratio;
(b) if so, the details of such institutions,
State-wise; and
(c) the action taken by Government to
press these institutions to maintain a
healthy staff-student ratio?
Differential fee structure in
professional courses
12. SHRI JANARDHANA
POOJARY:  Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether each State/UT has its
own fee structure for professional courses
like MBBS, Engineering and Architecture;
(b) if so, whether it is Rupees eighty
five thousand per annum for a B.E./
Architecture seat in one State, in another it
is Rupees thirty five to forty thousand;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) whether such high fees are beyond
the reach of students hailing from poor
families and rural areas;
(e) if so, whether Government would
set up a National Commission to frame a
reasonable and uniform fee structure
throughout the Country which is affordable
for the poor; and
(f) if so, the details thereof, and if not,
the reasons therefor?

4
World Bank funded projects for
upgrading education
13. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether World Bank funded projects
worth Rs. 1800 crore for upgrading
education facilities has run into rough
weather following turf war between the
officials of the Ministry of HRD;
(b) if so, the main projects affected and
the reasons therefor;
(c) by when Government would be able
to resolve this issue so that World Bank
funds for projects are available; and
(d) by when Government would be able
to utilize the funds fully?
Funds for U.P. under S.S.A.
14. SHRI LALIT SURI: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the funds allotted to the State of
Uttar Pradesh under Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan
for the year 2005-06;
(b) the extent to which the funds have
been utilized for the purpose during the
year;
(c) whether the balance, if any, would
be carried over to the next year;
(d) the funds allotted to the State under
this Abhiyan for the year 2006-07; and
(e) the number of students likely to be
benefited and the teachers proposed to be
trained under this Scheme in U.P. during
the year?
Financial assistance to State
Education Boards
15. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to refer to
the answer to Unstarred Question 3059
given in the Rajya Sabha on 15th May,
2006 and state:
(a) whether Government of
Maharashtra have since submitted request
for providing financial assistance to the
State Secondary and Higher Secondary
Boards which are giving quality education;
and
(b) if so, the action Government have
taken thereon?
Financial assistance for vocational
education and training
16. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to refer to
the answer to Unstarred Question 3058
given in the Rajya Sabha on 15th May,
2006 and state:
(a) whether the Government of
Maharashtra submitted necessary
justification and additional information in
connection with the financial assistance for
vocational education and training; and
(b) if so, the action Government have
taken thereon?
Free textbooks to students
17. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
of Andhra Pradesh is giving textbooks free
of cost to 1.05 crore students who are

5
studying in Government and aided schools
in the State;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether any such scheme is going
on at the Centre for giving textbooks free
of cost to poor and students studying in
Government and aided schools; and
(d) if not, the reasons for not adopting
the same and supplying free textbooks to
all students who are studying in
Government and aided schools?
Effectiveness of school education
system
18. SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that recently a
Committee has been set up to explore the
possibility of assessing the achievement of
students as an indicator of the effectiveness
and suitability of the school education
system in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof, including
the personnel of the Committee, the precise
terms of reference and the time-frame within
which the Committee would submit its
recommendations;
(c) whether any guidelines have been
suggested to help the Committee devise a
standardised system of achievement across
the schools and examination boards for
effecting improvement in school education;
and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Reservation of OBCs in IIMs
19. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether, in order to cope with
additional demand for IIM,  additional seats
are required for implementation of decision
for reservation of 27% seats for OBCs;
(b) whether Government has any
proposal in hand or under implementation
for setting up more IIMs; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Reservation for OBCs in medical
colleges
20. SHRIMATI  HEMA MALINI: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have taken a
decision to make effective 27 per cent
quota for OBCs in the medical colleges in
the country in spite of country-wide
agitation;
(b) whether it is not possible to create
additional seats equivalent of 27 per cent
quota as this will neither give scope for
further agitation for or against quota; and
(c) if so, the reaction of Government
thereto?
Uniform academic calendar
21. SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a proposal
has been drawn up by the University
Grants Commission to enforce a uniform
national academic calendar for all
universities which would lay down common
schedules for opening and closing of
universities and for holding examinations
and declaration of results;
(b) if so, the details of the proposal and
the views of different universities obtained,
if any, in view of the academic autonomy
enjoyed by the Central universities;
and

6
(c) whether and to what extent the
uniform calendar accommodates the
varying climatic conditions and holidays
observed on account of local festivals in
different parts of the country?
Opening of  ITIs in private sector
†22. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Planning
Commission has given a suggestion to the
Ministry of Human Resource Development
that permission should be granted to open
I.T.Is, in private sector keeping in view the
future technical requirement;
(b) if so, the decision taken by
Government in this regard; and
(c) by when the permission to open
I.T.Is in private sector will be granted?
Promotion of regional language by NBT
†23. SHRI PYARELAL
KHANDELWAL :  W ill the Minister of
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the role of
N.B.T. in propagation and promotion of
regional languages have been very dismal;
(b) whether it is also a fact that
Government have not made any efforts for
development of Punjabi language in
accordance with Rajiv-Longowal agreement;
(c) if not, the details of the efforts made
for Punjabi project during the last ten years
with special reference to the appointment
of employees; and
(d) the details of the efforts being made
for other regional languages, State-wise?
IIMs in Maharashtra
24. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: Will the
Minister of  HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are considering
to open more Indian Institutes of
Management (IIMs) and increase student
capacity in the established IIMs in the
country, particularly in Maharashtra
State;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Re-employment of superannuated
teachers
25. SHRIMATI HEMA MALINI: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is  a fact that Government
have asked the State Governments for re-
employment of superannuated teachers
upto the age of 65 in order to fill the teachers
posts in colleges and universities in the
country; and
(b) if so, the terms and conditions of
the re-employment of superannuated
teachers in the country?
Increase in seats in higher studies
26. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that as sequel to
implementation of reservation of OBC in
medical and other colleges of specialized
and higher studies from June 2007, the
number of seats in these colleges will be
increased;
(b) if so, the details of seats to be
increased in each college/institution;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

7
(c) whether this proposal has been
